The test image shows a soybean stem that is bleached white with large, dark black structures (sclerotia) visible on and within the stem tissue. The stem appears soft and degraded. These are hallmark features of White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot):

- **Bleached white stem** - characteristic of White Mold infection
- **Large black sclerotia** embedded in the stem - the defining diagnostic feature
- **Degraded, soft stem tissue** consistent with Sclerotinia infection

The White Mold reference images confirm this match, showing similar bleached stems with black sclerotia. Charcoal Rot was ruled out because its microsclerotia are much smaller (giving a speckled appearance), and Brown Stem Rot shows internal brown pith discoloration rather than bleached tissue with large sclerotia.
